From 1a307cc299430dd7139d351a3b8941f493dfa885 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nishanth Menon <nm@ti.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Feb 2022 14:10:06 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: ti: k3-j7200: Fix gic-v3 compatible regs

Though GIC ARE option is disabled for no GIC-v2 compatibility,
Cortex-A72 is free to implement the CPU interface as long as it
communicates with the GIC using the stream protocol. This requires
that the SoC integration mark out the PERIPHBASE[1] as reserved area
within the SoC. See longer discussion in [2] for further information.

Update the GIC register map to indicate offsets from PERIPHBASE based
on [3]. Without doing this, systems like kvm will not function with
gic-v2 emulation.

[1] https://developer.arm.com/documentation/100095/0002/system-control/aarch64-register-descriptions/configuration-base-address-register--el1
[2] https://lore.kernel.org/all/87k0e0tirw.wl-maz@kernel.org/
[3] https://developer.arm.com/documentation/100095/0002/way1382452674438

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d361ed88455f ("arm64: dts: ti: Add support for J7200 SoC")
Reported-by: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Nishanth Menon <nm@ti.com>
Acked-by: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220215201008.15235-4-nm@ti.com

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200.dtsi
index 64fef4e67d76..b6da0454cc5b 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200.dtsi
@@ -129,6 +129,7 @@ cbass_main: bus@100000 {
 			 <0x00 0x00a40000 0x00 0x00a40000 0x00 0x00000800>, /* timesync router */
 			 <0x00 0x01000000 0x00 0x01000000 0x00 0x0d000000>, /* Most peripherals */
 			 <0x00 0x30000000 0x00 0x30000000 0x00 0x0c400000>, /* MAIN NAVSS */
+			 <0x00 0x6f000000 0x00 0x6f000000 0x00 0x00310000>, /* A72 PERIPHBASE */
 			 <0x00 0x70000000 0x00 0x70000000 0x00 0x00800000>, /* MSMC RAM */
 			 <0x00 0x18000000 0x00 0x18000000 0x00 0x08000000>, /* PCIe1 DAT0 */
 			 <0x41 0x00000000 0x41 0x00000000 0x01 0x00000000>, /* PCIe1 DAT1 */
-- 
2.25.1



diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200-main.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200-main.dtsi
index 05a627ad6cdc..16684a2f054d 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200-main.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/k3-j7200-main.dtsi
@@ -54,7 +54,10 @@ gic500: interrupt-controller@1800000 {
 		#interrupt-cells = <3>;
 		interrupt-controller;
 		reg = <0x00 0x01800000 0x00 0x10000>,	/* GICD */
-		      <0x00 0x01900000 0x00 0x100000>;	/* GICR */
+		      <0x00 0x01900000 0x00 0x100000>,	/* GICR */
+		      <0x00 0x6f000000 0x00 0x2000>,	/* GICC */
+		      <0x00 0x6f010000 0x00 0x1000>,	/* GICH */
+		      <0x00 0x6f020000 0x00 0x2000>;	/* GICV */
 
 		/* vcpumntirq: virtual CPU interface maintenance interrupt */
 		interrupts = <GIC_PPI 9 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `k3-j7200.dtsi`**
   - Added a new entry to the `cbass_main` bus node to reserve the A72 PERIPHBASE address space:
     ```plaintext
     <0x00 0x6f000000 0x00 0x6f000000 0x00 0x00310000>, /* A72 PERIPHBASE */
     ```

2. **File: `k3-j7200-main.dtsi`**
   - Updated the `gic500` interrupt controller node to include additional GIC register mappings:
     - Added the following entries:
       ```plaintext
       <0x00 0x6f000000 0x00 0x2000>,	/* GICC */
       <0x00 0x6f010000 0x00 0x1000>,	/* GICH */
       <0x00 0x6f020000 0x00 0x2000>;	/* GICV */
       ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both files are related to the configuration of the GIC (Generic Interrupt Controller) for the J7200 SoC. The addition of the A72 PERIPHBASE in `k3-j7200.dtsi` establishes a reserved memory area necessary for the Cortex-A72 to communicate with the GIC using the stream protocol. The updates in `k3-j7200-main.dtsi` further define the GIC register mappings, ensuring that the GICD, GICR, GICC, GICH, and GICV registers are correctly addressed based on the newly reserved PERIPHBASE. Together, these changes are essential for proper GIC functionality and compatibility with systems like KVM that rely on GIC-v2 emulation.
